title: CLAY CITY SCHOOL BOARD
full_story:
The Clay City School Board met last night, ending the meeting with member Erin Boyd submitting her resignation.  Boyd is moving out of district.

Board members voted to direct Superintendent John Neubaum in consultation with legal counsel to develop a proposed non-binding advisory referendum question regarding exploring the deactivation of the High School for Board review and possible approval for placement on the ballot for the Spring 2027 Election.  A decision will have to be made by January 1st in order to put it on the March ballot.  Board member Mary Jo Patridge and Board president Misty Lindeman voted against the measure.  “I don’t believe the school should close and want nothing to do with these efforts,” Lindeman explained after the meeting.  Patridge said she had reasons for her vote but no public comment.  “I am not in favor of closing the high school, Superintendent Neubaum said.  “But the community has to make a commitment to keep it.  We have some building issues that will need to be addressed.  This is an overwhelming decision either way.”

In Superintendent Neubaum report enrollment totals 198 students with two new elementary, one new junior high and one new high school student.  Neubaum said the district has received tax money from Wayne County but not Clay County.  There have been attorney fees for three FOIA requests and expressed concerns about state money for transportation.  He said last year the district received $97,000 and this year only $57,000.  “I am concerned about how much we will receive next year for transportation,” Superintendent Neubaum commented.

Board member approved the FY-27 budget and a quote from Security Alarm for a new fire alarm interface and the replacement of smoke sensors and pull stations for $73,412.76.

In personnel action the board approved Beth Goodrum as elementary yearbook sponsor, Megan Billingsley as Senior class co-sponsor, Grace Collins and Kyia Sucher as Jr. High cheer sponsors, Nathan Deain as personal aide for Jr. High cross country, Courtney Mitchell as Assistant basketball coach, and approval of hiring a temporary custodian through a staffing agency.

title: FLORA HIGH SCHOOL HOMECOMING
full_story:

title: APPLEKNOCKER 26
full_story:
The Flora Academic Foundation Appleknocker will be held tomorrow from 9:30 to 2:30 pm at the Flora Elementary School.  There will be free entertainment, great food and fun and games for all ages.

Activities will begin at 9:30 with flag raising ceremonies with the Shooting Stars Drill Team.  The Flora High School Band under the direction of Ethan Steber, will perform at 9:45 followed by DAS-zle Dance and Tumble at 10:30 pm in the FES multipurpose room.  From 11 to 1 a youth open mic hosted by Matt Lovett will take place on the outside stage.  Power and Grace Tumbling and Dance will perform at 1 pm inside the FES multipurpose room.

Food and Games will be onsite all day, the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders will have a pedal tractor pull and Clay County emergency vehicles will be available for tours, and there will be a hands-on robotics display.  Parking will be available at the Football Field.  The festival will close at 2:30 pm.

The Flora Academic Foundation provides financial support to supplement, enrich, and enhance quality programs and educational opportunities for the children of the Flora Unit School District.  Visit the FAF/Appleknocker link on the flora school website for more information.

title: CLAY COUNTY PROPERTY TAXES
full_story:
Clay County Real Estate tax bills were mailed on Friday, September 11th.

The first installment of the 2025 taxes payable in 2026 is due in 3 weeks on Friday, October 16th.  The second installment is due on Friday, November 20th.

Payment can be made to the Clay County Treasurer using any of the following options, by mail, send your check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville, IL 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.  You can pay at the treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse where they accept cash, checks, cashier’s checks, or money orders.  Please bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  Office hours are 8:00 am – 4:00 pm Monday through Friday.  Online payments can be made by credit/debit card by going to govpaynow.com PLC #a00082, there will be a convenience fee charged for online Credit Card payments.  Payment can also be made by placing your payment in the envelope depository at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.

For questions call Clay County Treasurer Stacey Allen’s office at 618-665-3727.

title: NORTH WAYNE BOARD
full_story:
The North Wayne School Board met Wednesday night.  They held a budget hearing prior to the regular board meeting.  During the budget hearing the FY27 budget was approved.

A motion was made stating that if the North Wayne Board of Education decides to proceed with a plan to close both elementary schools and build a new elementary school in front of Cisne Middle School then the board will adopt a resolution in time to include the resolution on the April 6th, ballot to be voted on by the taxpayers in the district.  The motion failed 4-2.  The board has been in discussion with BLDD Architects to close both Mt. Erie and Johnsonville schools and consolidate into a new Pre K through 8 facility at a cost of $9.6 million.

The Board approved the 2025 – 26 Administrator and Teacher Salary and Benefits Report, the purchase of new AED machines as needed, and the FY26 audit as presented by Kemper CPA Group.  They also gave Superintendent Adam Ellis approval to apply for the FY27 School Maintenance Project Grant.

In personnel matters the board accepted the letter of resignation submitted by Sonia Allen as Cisne Middle School Cafeteria Assistant.

title: ISP URGES HOMECOMING SAFETY
full_story:
The Illinois State Police (ISP) reminds teens and their families to enjoy homecoming celebrations responsibly this year because the choices made today can have lasting consequences.

In July 2026, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) published its Young Driver Traffic Safety Fact Sheet, which showed young people between the ages of 15 and 20 years old, accounted for 9% of all drivers involved in a fatal traffic crash.  The Fact Sheet also showed 53% of young drivers killed were not wearing a seatbelt and 29% had alcohol in their system.  In Illinois, the leading contributing causes of major injury and fatal crashes are commonly referred to as “fatal four” violations; impaired driving, speeding, distracted driving, and improper seatbelt usage.

“ISP is doing its part to help prevent tragedies this homecoming season through increased traffic enforcement and patrols, but also through safety education,” said ISP Director Brendan F. Kelly.  “We encourage parents and guardians to discuss the dangers of alcohol and drug use with their children, including not getting in a car with a driver who has been consuming drugs or alcohol.”

Illinois is a zero-tolerance state when it comes to underage drinking, it is illegal for any person under the age of 21 to possess or consume any amount of an alcoholic beverage.  Violators may be cited, fined, or arrested, and vehicles will be towed.

In addition to staying sober, young drivers should follow the speed limit, wear their seatbelts, even in the backseat, and avoid phone use and other distractions while driving.  Illinois law prohibits cellphone usage for young drivers under age 19, including a hands-free device, except to call law enforcement or emergency services.

The ISP Safety Education Unit offers a wide variety of free educational programs for schools and community groups throughout Illinois.  For more information on the programs offered, visit https://isp.illinois.gov/TrafficSafety/SafetyEducation or email [email protected].

Cheer for your team and have fun at the big dance, but do so responsibly and get home safely.

title: EFFINGHAM MAN SENTENCED
full_story:
Attorney General Kwame Raoul announced an Effingham man was sentenced to 38 years in prison for producing child sexual abuse material.  The case is part of Raoul’s ongoing work, in collaboration with federal law enforcement agencies and local law enforcement officials throughout Illinois, to apprehend offenders who download and trade child sexual abuse material online.

Landin Miller, 24, was sentenced in Effingham County Circuit Court after pleading guilty to two counts of video production of child sexual abuse material, both Class X felonies; and two counts of still shot production of child sexual abuse material, both Class 1 felonies.

In May 2024, Raoul’s investigators, along with officers from the Effingham Police Department, conducted a search of Miller’s residence.  He was taken into custody and charged after investigators discovered evidence of child sexual abuse material.

Raoul’s office co-prosecuted this case with Effingham County State’s Attorney Aaron Jones’ office.

Raoul’s office, with a grant from the US Department of Justice, runs the Illinois Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force that investigates child exploitation crimes and trains law enforcement agencies.  The task force receives CyberTips, or online reports of child sexual abuse material, from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children.  Over the last several years, CyberTipline reports have steadily increased.  In 2025, reports to the ICAC Task Force increased by 45% over 2024.

title: KINMUNDY LOG CABIN VILLAGE
full_story:
The annual Fall Festival at the Kinmundy Log Cabin Village is tomorrow and Sunday, at the Kinmundy Log Cabin Village on Gesell Road.  The Fall Festival offers visitors a chance to step back in time while enjoying a full weekend of family fun.

Admission is five dollars, with children five and under admitted free.  Festival hours are 10 am to 5 pm on Saturday and 10 am to 4 pm on Sunday.

The event features more than 150 craft and food vendors, along with live demonstrations and plenty of activities for the entire family.  Visitors can also explore the village’s collection of historic 1800s log cabins while enjoying the sights, sounds and flavors of the fall season.

The Kinmundy Log Cabin Village is located at 6260 Gesell Road in Kinmundy. For more information, visit kinmundylogcabinvillage.com.

title: EIU GETS NATIONAL RECOGNITION
full_story:
Eastern Illinois University received national and regional recognition for affordability, academic programs and student outcomes.

Last week, Time magazine and research partner Statista named EIU to its “America’s Best Colleges of 2026-2027” list.  The university said the recognition reflects its commitment to affordability, academic offerings, graduation rates and post-graduation success.

EIU is the only Ohio Valley Conference institution included on the list.

The university also earned a “Best Value University” designation in the Midwest from US News & World Report.  EIU said the recognition highlights its focus on making college affordable while supporting positive outcomes for students.

In addition, OnlineCybersecurity.org ranked EIU’s online cybersecurity program as the top public program in Illinois in its 2027 listings.

Those interested in visiting campus can register online. For more information, contact the EIU Office of Admissions at 217-581-2224 or [email protected].
